lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles
lessonRef.title: Assessment preparation: the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12 and hypotenuse 13. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 5. Find cos θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
A right triangle has hypotenuse 15 and one leg 9. Find the other leg.
Express sin 32° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 148°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 122°, because the angles differ by a right angle
cos 58°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 32°, because sine and cosine are always equal

items.prompt: From a point 4 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 3 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
choices: cos θ = 3/4
sin θ = 3/4
tan θ = 3/4
tan θ = 4/3

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 10 and 24 and hypotenuse 26. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 10. Find sin θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.

choices: cos 166°, because the angles differ by a right angle
